Welcome to The Compass School
The Compass School Vision
Welcome to The Compass School
Welcome to The Compass School. As a small school for pupils with social, emotional and mental health needs, we provide a broad and balanced curriculum. Alongside this, we offer bespoke support for our pupils’ mental health and wellbeing and help for pupils to understand themselves and their emotions.

Headteacher’s Welcome
Hello and a very warm welcome to The Compass School, a school for students with social, emotional and mental health needs.
Situated near Romford, we are incredibly proud to have opened this school in Havering and we look forward to making a positive contribution to our local community.
Our school has come alive as a community now that our pupils, families and staff have been working with us since September 2023 to build a great future.
We provide an education where young people can flourish and teach academic subjects in line with the National Curriculum, as well as providing a bespoke, nurturing environment to prepare our learners to lead fulfilling lives.
The success of this school is down to the people who are in it and who support it – extraordinary people doing extraordinarily good things.
Catharine Wensley, Headteacher.

pageCache.text:
Vision, Values and Mission
Vision
‘True navigation begins in the human heart’
Our ambition is to unlock the potential of all children because every young life is special.
We want students to leave The Compass School open to possibility and gifted with the potential to change the world for the better.
We have high expectations of all students and believe that with the right support every student can succeed at The Compass School.
Our school provides a compass to guide the children and young people in our care: ‘True navigation begins in the human heart. It is the most important map of all’.
Each journey through life is unique.
Starting from different places, we travel with others but we each discover our own way through the challenges life brings.
We will educate and guide our pupils to successfully travel their path to adulthood.
Values
Our School Star Values:
⭐ We strive to be the best that we can be – understanding ourselves and our unique contribution to our community.
⭐ We produce the best work that we can so that we feel proud of ourselves.
⭐ We are committed to equality and understand and value diversity – success for all.
⭐ We understand that we will achieve more together than we can alone.
⭐ We value kindness and build trust We are honest with ourselves and each other fostering mutual respect.
⭐ We respect and develop ourselves, our community and our environment.
⭐ We champion the potential in everyone.
⭐ We work towards leading healthy and fulfilled lives.
⭐ We keep trying, even when things are hard.
⭐ We learn from our mistakes and believe we can improve.
⭐ We know how to handle stressful situations.
Our Staff Working Partnership – How We Work
⭐ Embracing the vision.
⭐ Putting our pupils always first.
⭐ Being honest and acting with integrity.
⭐ Practising respect for one another.
⭐ Pulling together at all times.
⭐ Supporting our operating rules and culture.
⭐Working safely and responsibly.
Mission to support pupils with SEMH
We aim to provide an education which delivers outstanding outcomes for children with social, emotional and mental health needs.
Underpinning this are high expectations and aspirations for all, so we ensure that all children make good progress from whatever their starting points and are supported to achieve accreditation and qualifications which enhance their life chances.
We will ensure that children have positive destinations to move on to in the next stage of their lives. We believe it is essential children experience a ‘rite of passage’ through which they can grow and develop increasing maturity towards that goal. We will make links with local employers, apprenticeship opportunities and Further Education and Higher Education providers.
For this reason, we shall establish three phases in the school: a Key Stage 2 phase, a Key Stage 3 phase and a Key Stage 4 phase. Each of these phases will have distinctive features and an appropriate curriculum offer.
Reading lies at the heart of our academic curriculum and we determined that our students will leave us able with the reading, writing and communication skills they need to flourish: ‘We believe, as articulated through ‘The reading framework: Teaching the foundations of literacy’ (DFE July 2021) that:
Reading is fundamental to education. Proficiency in reading, writing and spoken language is vital for pupils’ success. Through these, they develop communication skills for education and for working with others’.
Within the phases we shall combine a strong curriculum offer with multi-agency and therapeutic support and we shall work in partnership with Havering Local Authority and other local providers to deliver this.
The curriculum will be organised to educate the whole person: head, heart and hands, based on Pestalozzi’s educational philosophy: students will have the chance to think and develop their academic and intellectual abilities to care about other and explore and understand their emotions and explore moral attitudes and they will experience practical activities and develop their social skills, character and common sense.

About Us
Welcome to The Compass School.
As of September 2025, we are now in our third year and have expanded into primary with a Year 4/5 and Year 6 class, and going up to year 11.
As a small school for pupils with social, emotional and mental health needs, we provide a broad and balanced curriculum, alongside bespoke support for our pupils’ mental health and wellbeing and help for pupils to understand themselves and their emotions.
This support is woven into our school day through our trauma-informed approach to working with our pupils. This year, we are further developing our enrichment offer and planning more trips and visits after our amazing school trip to Stubbers at the end of the summer term. We want all our pupils to enjoy their time at The Compass School and to experience a wide range of opportunities beyond the classroom-based curriculum.
We will continue to grow over the coming years and will have a primary phase (Key Stage Two) and a secondary phase for pupils in Key Stage Three (11-14) and Key Stage Four (14-16). We will have 24 places for pupils at Key Stage Two, 24 places for pupils at Key Stage Three and 22-24 places for Key Stage Four. We have space for up to 60 pupils.
This is a very exciting time to join us, as a pupil or as a member of staff and we look forward to welcoming you to one of our regular open events, if you want to find out more about us.

We have high expectations of all students and believe that with the right support every student can succeed at The Compass School, enabling them to contribute to society and live healthy and fulfilled lives.
At The Compass School, our Personal Development Curriculum runs alongside the Academic Curriculum.
The Personal Development Curriculum focusses on the five aspects of human experience that keeps us all well:
We all need to be well in ourselves and to feel that our presence is a positive force for good for others. We strive to re-engage students and their families and to create strong, positive relationships and to support children to meet their EHCP targets.
We are ambitious to for our students and the overall aim is to use any interventions for the shortest period of time necessary and to evaluate their impact at least half-termly. We know that the best experience at school comes from high-quality teaching in the classroom.
Our vision is for our pupils to contribute to society and live healthy and fulfilled lives: the wellness curriculum will provide the foundations for pupils to achieve this goal.
Connecting with others (communication and interaction)
New learning (learning which is child-focused)
Being prepared for life
The Personal Development Curriculum is underpinned by our trauma perceptive practice and our determination that our students will develop the resilience to meet increasing demands over time, so that they are prepared for life. Restorative justice is one of the ways in which we support students to understand consequences and develop their resilience by asking them to consider the impact of their behaviour on others and to put things right.
The curriculum is planned to start from activities with the lowest level of demand and build resilience over time – for example, starting with playing a board game with chosen peers and building up to taking part in a group activity with pupils from another school.
The Personal Development Curriculum is planned to meet individual needs and to remove barriers for individuals. The five areas of the curriculum also help everyone to be mentally healthy and we will support all pupils to continue to be active, to connect, to take notice, to learn new things and to contribute through our PSHE curriculum.
The curriculum is organised around our STAR values (success, teamwork, aspiration and resilience) so that pupils can understand what these mean in practice and show how they are living the values in their daily lives.

Academic Curriculum
Our Vision for the Curriculum
The curriculum at The Compass School is a seven-year journey.
Our pupils study a broad and balanced curriculum with the intention of preparing them for a world we cannot imagine and making sure they are ready for adult life and the next stages of their education, employment or training.
There are no limits placed on their achievements. Wider opportunities are provided through our enrichment programme and the STAR Pledge.
Our curriculum is based on an academically rigorous offer which will be delivered with the expertise of staff trained to understand how to meet the needs of our cohort with Social Emotional and Mental Health needs.
We will go the extra mile to engage pupils and scaffold learning so that everyone achieves their best.
We know that great teaching, every lesson, every day, transforms lives.
We have chosen curriculum plans which enable us to support learners who need to secure threshold concepts and key knowledge and skills by using the well-planned resources from earlier stages of the curriculum where necessary.
Success
All children undertake carefully sequenced programmes of study across the full range of traditional school disciplines – English, Mathematics, the Sciences, the Humanities, Religious Studies, Creative and Performing Arts, IT and Design Technology and Sport.
Reading lies at the heart of our academic curriculum and we are determined that our students will leave us with the reading, writing and communication skills they need to flourish. We believe:
“Reading is fundamental to education. Proficiency in reading, writing and spoken language is vital for pupils’ success. Through these, they develop communication skills for education and for working with others.”
They also have wider opportunities to learn about the world and to contribute to the community.
Every child matters and we strive to ensure that every child thrives in their lessons and takes full part in the wider curriculum on offer. We provide the therapeutic curriculum and necessary targeted interventions to support every pupil to access their learning.
Teamwork
We are a community which prepares young people to take their place in the world where they can hold formal and informal conversations with confidence, take part in dialogic learning and work together to solve problems, hold restorative conversations and reach resolutions.
Fundamental British Values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs, and for those without faith, are explored and supported through our curriculum – including our PSHE programme, form time curriculum and assemblies – so our pupils are prepared to work with their communities to make a positive contribution in their adult lives.
Aspiration
We want our children to be happy and to feel positive about themselves, their time at school and their futures.
We have a carefully planned PSHE and RSE curriculum where children learn about how to look after themselves and each other.
Pupils learn that they can fully participate in the life of the school and the wider community through Student Council, voluntary work and extra-curricular activities. Our careers programme inspires them to aspire and to see the many opportunities available to them.
Resilience
All pupils are trained to study independently and to develop a ‘Growth Mindset’.
We know a lot about how young people learn and teach them about self-regulation; self-efficacy and meta-cognition. We plan learning so that pupils retain knowledge in their long-term memories.
Teachers provide pupils with an overview of the curriculum topics and content for each half term. Assessment criteria, success criteria and model answers are shared with students and feedback is provided to ensure that all pupils know what they need to do to improve their work or fill any gaps in their understanding and can learn to do this without adult support.

Our Curriculum
The Compass School aims to provide a broad, balanced, and therapeutic curriculum that removes barriers to learning, fostering resilience, emotional regulation, and academic progress. It prioritizes social-emotional development alongside academic knowledge, empowering pupils to achieve EHCP outcomes and qualifications.

Having fun in the last week(s) at The Compass School before our summer break
Published: 3 July, 2026
Transition Day – welcoming our new pupils and staff
Our first exciting day as we wind down for the summer break is our Transition Day!
On Thursday 9th July we welcomed our new pupils and staff, and everyone got to meet their new class September class team. It was such a good day and it was lovely meeting our new pupils. Hopefully it helped take away some of the September anxiety.
Summer Fete
Heading into our final week, we held a summer fete for our parents to visit the school at 2pm, to see our school and say goodbye to staff for the summer, as well as buy our pupils’ home made merchandise. All money raised will go back into the budget to organise fun events for next year.
Our fetes are always very popular amongst pupils, parents and staff, and it’s always a joy to see the school bustling with parents and other family members. Once again, our pupils excelled in selling their creations and it was a lovely afternoon.
Sports Day
On Wednesday 15th July we held our Sports Day. Once again, we had some really good engagement from pupils, staff and parents – and most importantly, no injuries!
Parents were invited to join us to their child’s class slot and it was great to see our pupils’ families come to support them.
Stubbers Activity Centre
On the second to last day of term, Thursday 16th July, we went on our annual day out to Stubbers Activity Centre. Both staff and pupils get to push their boundaries and explore new activities, often daring to do things they didn’t think they could!
Again, we had excellent weather and it’s a long but rewarding day out for all, making it a great end to the academic year.

If you are worried about any child in our school and think that they may be the victim of neglect, abuse or cruelty, then please speak to a member of our team who then ensure appropriate next steps are then taken.

Schools and their staff form part of the wider safeguarding system for children. Everyone who comes into contact with children and their families and carers has a role to play in keeping them safe. To fulfil this responsibility effectively, all professionals must ensure their approach is child-centred. This means that they must always consider what is in the best interests of the child.
At The Compass School our role is to meet the safeguarding and child protection needs of pupils with social, emotional and mental health needs.
